issues.detail: Active Work.Request names `src/tags.js` explicitly. A run could read this as a persisted target area and choose subtree mode instead of gapfill. The stale claims (runtime, test command) are project-level and src/tags.js needs no refresh, so gapfill remains the defensible choice. The judge may still see some ambiguity.
issues.fix: Optionally reword the request in layers/30-cycle/.standards/STATE.md to 'Replace the hand-written set helpers with the built-in Set methods and keep the existing tests passing.' This removes the subtree temptation. Note that the slug-based cycle ID would then no longer match the request perfectly, though check.mjs does not enforce that.

issues.detail: The `contains npm run test:unit` check, also used for assertion 2, assumes the refreshed Commands entry names the npm invocation rather than only the script name `test:unit` or the raw `node --test` command. This is the established invocation in the README and CI and is quoted in the case, so a correct run will almost certainly reproduce it.
issues.fix: None needed. If the check misfires, relax it to `test:unit`.

summary: The fixture realizes every stated condition. A usable CONTEXT.md is stale only on the Node 20 / `npm test` claims, while package.json, .nvmrc, CI, and README establish Node 22 and `npm run test:unit`, and the state is a clean STANDARD AUDITING cycle with AuditTarget NONE and check.mjs ok.
